21. In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused being the driver of the Car drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident due to which the victim succumbed to death and prosecution contended that acc

Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused C.C.No.4111/2021 was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to a
For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness or error of judgment.

The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/do

22. In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the
23. In the instant case the prosecution has examined 8 witnesses to prove their case.
Among them P.W.1 is the complainant who is an hearsay witness, P.W.2 to 4 are the eye witnesses, P.W.5 is the mahazar witness, and P.W.6 to 8 are the investigating officers.
In the instant case the prosecution is relying on P.W.2 to 4 i.e., eye witnesses and investigating officer.

The learned C.C.No.4111/2021 APP contended that all the eye witnesses supported their case and their evidence is corroborated with the evidence of investigating officer and they have proved their case as per their version.
24. In the instant case the accused is the driver of the alleged vehicle the said fact is not disputed by the defence.
The defence also did not dispute the alleged accident between the Dio scooter and creta car.
25. To prove the rash and negligent act of the accused the prosecution has relied its case on P.W.2 to 4.
P.W.2 in his chief examination deposed that the accused driver drove his car in a rash and negligent manner.
He did not explain in what manner the car was driven and what is the negligence which he has noticed.
The other eye witness deposed that the accused drove his car in high speed and dashed to two wheeler.
The P.W.4 did not depose anything about either high speed or negligence she simply deposed that the accused came in opposite direction and dashed to their scooter.

To bring home the culpability of accused under section 279 and 304(A) IPC, it is necessary to know the relevant provisions of law which reads as follows:
Section 279. Rash driving or riding on a public way:
Whoever drives any vehicle, or ri
27. Upon bare perusal of the above provision in order to come to conclusion that accused has committed the offence punishable under above section, the prosecution must establish the following:

7
1. Person must be driving or riding vehicle in a public way.
2. He must be driving in a rash and negligent manner.
3. He must be driving in a manner likely to endanger human life or personal safety of any person.
28. Upon plain reading of the provision of law i.e., Sec.279 and 304 (A) of IPC , the prosecution has to make out that death is a direct consequence of a rash or C.C.No.4111/2021 negligent act.
As per dictionary meaning Rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or doing an act without due consideration whereas negligence connotes want of proper care.

A rash act implies an act done by a person with recklessness or with indifference to its consequences, the prosecution must establish that the alleged accused must be conscious of his act and must be aware of the consequences which will tak
A negligent act, refers to an act done by a person without taking sufficient precautions or reasonable precautions to avoid its probable mischievous or illegal consequences.
The prosecution has contended that accused has committed negligent act due to which the rider of the motor cycle was succumbed to death.

29. With regard to negligent act the Hon'ble Apex court in "Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs State of Andhra Pradesh (decided on 28.07.2000)" , wherein the Court discussed in detail the constituents of a "rash or negligent act" and observed:
"A
It is opposed to a deliberate act.
Still a rash act can be a deliberate act in the sense that it was done without due care and caution.
Culpable rashness lies in running the risk of doing an act with recklessness and with indifference as to the consequences.
Criminal negligence is the failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and C.C.No.4111/2021 precaution guarding against injury to the public generally or to any individual in particular.
It is the imperative duty of the driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution."

30. Further, in the case of "Braham Dass Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh (2009) 3 SCC (Cri) 406",
while discussing the legal position with respect to an offence u/s 279/304A, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, interalia observed the followin
Similarly, in Section 304A the stress is on causing death by negligence or rashness.
Therefore, for bringing in application of either Section 279 or 304A it must be established that there was an element of rashness or negligence.
Even if the prosecution version is accepted in toto, there was no evidence led to show that any negligence was involved."
31. In the instant case, the fact that the accused was driving the vehicle has not been disputed by him and he has not deposed anything in his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C.

Thus, it is Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
8 not in dispute that accused Shreyas was driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.
Now the prosecution has the burden to prove the rashness and negligence on the part of the accused.
To prove the same they have examined P.W.2 to 4 and relied on them.
PW.2 is the eye witness who deposed that he was standing in front of his shop at the time fo accident and he has seen the accident from a distance of 20ft.
He contended accused drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
He contended that the accident has taken place at a distance of 5ft from the left side edge of the road.
He disputed the rough sketch map which was prepared by the investigating officer and deposed in clarity that the accident spot is shown in wrong place.
Unfortunately he is a witness to the spot mahazar and rough sketch as well.
According to him accident has taken place at a distance of 15ft from the edge of the road which means exactly in the center of the road.
The said witness in his crossexamination also deposed about damage caused to the auto.
He deposed about presence of auto at accident spot and involvement of auto in the accident spot.
If auto is damaged why it has been not shown in the charge sheet.
What constrained the investigating officer from examining the driver of the said auto.
He is a material witness to the case of the prosecution.
The said witness is not listed in the prosecution witness list.
Which raises doubt about the investigation of the case.
The same witness in his cross examination clearly admits it is a two way road and normally the road is busy and it has high density of C.C.No.4111/2021 traffic.
If that is the scenario what is the negligence on the part of the accused, nothing is deposed by the said witness.
When he himself admits the accident has taken place in the center of the road, if the same is considered in feets it is exactly the center lane and not a inch excess to their lane.
The prosecution failed to establish the negligence on the part of the accused driver from this witness.
Moreover a doubt is created with the inclusion of auto into the scene.
33. P.W.3 the other eye witness deposed that the accused drove his vehicle in high speed and dashed to two wheeler which was coming from opposite direction.
Apart from high speed he did not mention anything about negligence.
Whether high speed alone constitutes negligence Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled "State of Karnataka Vs. Satish ((1998) 8 SCC 493)"

wherein the Apex Court observed:
"merely because the truck was being driven at a high speed does not bespeak of either "negligence or rashness" by itself.
None of the witness examined by the prosecution could give any indication, even approximately, as to what they meant by "high speed".
High speed is a relative term.
It was for the prosecution to bring on record material to establish as to what it meant by high speed in the facts and circumstances of the case.

In a criminal trial, the burden of providing everything essential to the establishment of the charge against an accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of C.C.No.4111/2021 the accused until
Criminality is not to be presumed subject of course to some statutory exceptions.
There is no statutory exception pleaded in the present case.

Rajajinagar Trps vs Shreyas S M on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153729137/
9
In the absence of any material on record, no presumption of rashness or negligence could be drawn by invoking the maxim "res ipsa loquitur".

34. In the above said judgment the court has clearly held that mere driving the vehicle in high speed will not amounts to negligence and it is for the prosecution to prove how high speed amounts to negligence.

In the case on hand the same witness who deposed about high speed also deposed that the said road where accident has taken place is having a width of 30ft and the said road is a busy road and normally has heavy traffic.
When there is a heavy traffic the question of driving the vehicle in high speed is not possible.

moreover it is not the case of the prosecution that the accused was so negligent that he drove his vehicle in high speed in a busy road and caused damages to several vehicles in one act, if that is the scenario the version of the prosecutio
Unfortunately nothing of such kind is placed before the court and the prosecution did not include the auto which was damaged in the alleged accident.
The other eye witness P.W.4 did not depose anything about the negligence on the part of the accused driver.
. Further the prosecution has to prove that the alleged negligent act of the accused is the direct cause of death.
The investigating officer did not depose anything about the possession of driving license by the deceased at the time of the accident.
There is no mention whether the rider or the pillion rider was wearing a head gear at the time of accident.
According to postmortem report the death is a result of head injury sustained.
If the said person wear a helmet then there is a chance of avoiding head injury, the prosecution did not place any materials about wearing the head gear.
36. Further aspect is the victim fell on the footpath after the collusion.
As per prosecution sketch map i.e., Ex.P.4 the footpath is at distance of 7ft from the accident spot.
Upon perusal of photographs there is a grill over the footpath, whether the victim fly in the air and landed on the footpath and sustained heady injury, none of the witness spoken about the same.
Everybody speaks about colluding with the footpath stone, how she landed on footpath, whether the grills came in between the deceased and footpath there is no clarity.
These factors raises doubt about the version of the prosecution itself.
The other aspect with regard to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Admittedly the deceased is a girl and rider is also a girl, there is a doubt whether they possess valid driving license and she is riding a high speed vehicle.
The counsel further contended the deceased was riding a unfit vehicle and due to his negligence the untoward incident has taken place.
38. Whether the prosecution has established rash and negligent act on the part of the accused.

In that regard the Hon'ble Apex court in S. Khader v. N. Gama, has held that the the important criteria for deciding as to whether the driver who caused the accident was rash or negligent would depend upon some of the following factors : Th

2 . Width of the road;
3. Density of the traffic; and 4. Attempt, if any to overtake the vehicles.

39. Upon perusal of the records of the instant case though the witness speak about high speed of the vehicle they did not speak about any attempt to over take C.C.No.4111/2021 the other vehicle by accused person.
Further all most all witnesses admit about high density of traffic on the said road.
Which generally raises a presumption that high speed is not possible particularly with regard to four wheeler.
Since it consumes more space for passing and violation of the same gathers attention of the general public.
Admittedly the said road is quite wider enough for movement of large vehicles, it has a width of 30ft and it is a two way road without any divider.

As per the admissions there is a commercial establishment on both sides and there is a provision for parking of vehicles as well, if that aspect is taken into consideration the width of the road is reduced from both sides and it congest the
According to witness the accident has taken place in the middle of the road and according to prosecution it is a head to head collusion.
On perusal of the sketch map as per Ex.P.4 the victim has not crossed the center line and it is the accused crossed the center line.
As discussed earlier their is a contradiction on this aspect.
Negligence is the absence of care and caution whereas culpable rashness results from lack of circumspection.
Merely because the car is being driven at a high speed it would be speak of either negligence or rashness.
High speed is a relative term and that has to be examined in the light of the facts & circumstances of the C.C.No.4111/2021 case.
In the instant case though they speak about speed of the accused none of them speak about the speed of the victim.
With the available materials the court cannot come to the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to the speed of the accused alone.
40. The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.
Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to show his involvement.
Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt.
Since the prosecution is relying on the interested witnesses the credential value of the interested witness without independent witness is of no use unless corroborated by other material witness.
In the instant case the prosecution did not examined any material or independent eye witnesses to prove its case.
41. Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
There is doubt as to whether the accused had driven the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to C.C.No.4111/2021 endanger the human life and personal safety of others.

Therefore, in the circumstances of the case,
as per the rules of criminal justice if any doubt arise about the commission of the act then such doubt shall be in favour of accused.
The prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
Accordingly, the points under consideration are answered point No.1 and 2 IN THE NEGATIVE.
POINT No.3:

In view of the above discussions and findings I proceed to pass the following ORDER Acting U/sec. 255(1) of Criminal procedure code, the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against him punishable U/sec. 279 and 304(A) of IPC
Bail bonds of accused and surety bonds shall stand canceled after completion of appeal period.
